relevance.rationale: Andersen-Mistegard, resurgence analysis of quantum invariants of Seifert fibered homology spheres. Its Theorem 2 states that the poles of the Borel transform of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X) coincide with the classical complex Chern-Simons values, and Theorem 3 that the GPPV q-series Z-hat_0(X;q) is a Borel-Laplace resummation of Z_0(X). The corpus applies exactly this principle heuristically: rem:ohtsuki-tower-bar-parity asserts that the Borel-Pade resummation of the odd (Gevrey-1) Ohtsuki sub-tower has its Borel singularity at the real action A = Vol(4_1)/pi, off the imaginary integration ray, hence no Stokes ambiguity -- a statement about where Borel singularities sit relative to complex-CS actions. So the paper supplies the theorem-form of a principle the corpus uses. It is NOT core, and deliberately not aid-proof: the results are proved for Seifert fibered homology spheres, a class the corpus contains no member of, whereas the corpus's object is a hyperbolic knot complement (4_1). Transporting the pole-location theorem across that gap is precisely what would need checking, and this document does not do it.

keyResults.statement: For a Seifert fibered homology sphere X, the poles of the Borel transform of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X) coincide with the set of classical complex Chern-Simons values CS_C(X).
keyResults.useForFolio: A proved instance of 'Borel singularities sit at complex CS actions', the assumption behind the corpus's placement of the Ohtsuki-tower Borel singularity at Vol(4_1)/pi; usable as corroboration of the principle and as the statement whose hypotheses a knot-complement transfer would have to reproduce.

keyResults.statement: Z-hat_0(X;q) is a Borel-Laplace resummation of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X), with a full asymptotic expansion as q -> exp(2 pi i / k) recovering the WRT invariant tau_k(X).
keyResults.useForFolio: The resummation-side template for the corpus's open multi-instanton / median-resummation residual on the one-instanton normalization (the quantitatively open leg of the u(q_0) map).

proposedActions.rationale: Named in two beans (rt2f, s013) as 'Seifert resurgence machinery' but has no ref() entry.

Record that the Borel-poles = complex-CS-values statement is PROVED only for Seifert fibered homology spheres, and state what a transfer to the 4_1 complement would require, so the corpus's heuristic placement of the Ohtsuki-tower Borel singularity is not read as literature-backed.

The corpus's Borel-Pade probe locates a singularity at A = Vol(4_1)/pi ~ 0.646; Thm 2 says (in its own class) such singularities are exactly complex-CS actions. Cross-checking the probe's numerically located singularity against the 4_1 complex-CS spectrum is a cross-check to run, not a number to adopt.
